title: Barbell Bench Press
summary: A flat barbell press for the chest, front delts and triceps, and the main upper-body strength lift.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: barbell (Olympic bar); weight plates; rack with J-hooks (power rack, squat stands or bench uprights); flat bench.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for chest (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly chest total.
Library rating 0.5 for front delts (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly front delts total.
Library rating 0.5 for triceps (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly triceps total.

setup.text: Lie with your eyes under the bar and your feet flat. Pull your shoulder blades back and down.
Grip a little wider than your shoulders and unrack the bar over your shoulders.
Lower it under control to your mid-chest, with your elbows about 45–70° from your body.
Press back up and slightly back toward your face until your arms are straight.

form_cues.cue: Lower the bar to your mid-chest
Keep elbows about 45 degrees from your torso
Press up and slightly back over the shoulders
Keep your shoulder blades pinned and your butt on the bench the whole time.

mistakes.text: Bouncing the bar off your chest instead of touching and pressing.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds two or three ramp-up sets at rising loads before the first working set, unless that load is very light.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 6-10 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Set safety arms or pins where you can fail a rep safely, or use a spotter, and use collars.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.
